reason: The hypothesis relies on specific claims about entropy-driven selective oxidation and suppression of non-protective oxides, but the cited evidence does not address configurational entropy effects. E1 notes the absence of Cr2O3 led to Mn oxide formation, and E2 describes general oxidation behavior of Cr and Al without linking to entropy, leaving key premises unsupported.
premises: High configurational entropy minimizes local segregation and stably disperses elements
Al and/or Cr oxidize preferentially in the HEA matrix to form a continuous protective oxide layer
The protective oxide layer acts as a barrier that slows oxygen ingress and outward diffusion of non-protective elements (e.g., Mn)
Suppression of less protective oxides (e.g., Mn oxides) is a direct consequence of the selective oxidation promoted by high entropy
